signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + NFP Miss + Geopolitical Catalyst
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.82, breaking below its SMA20/50 cluster as the dollar index drops to a 7-week low under 100.00. US July non-farm payrolls surprised at -23K vs +80K expected, triggering a bull steepener in the US yield curve with the 2Y yield plunging -59bp. The JPY 1W avg outperformance of +1.242% (n=7) makes it the G10 leader, while CHF lags at -0.756%, creating a critical 1.998% G10 spread. Despite a 275bp Fed-BoJ OIS carry advantage for USD, soft US labor data and easing Hormuz geopolitical tensions are forcing a rapid carry unwind. Options markets confirm the downside bias with a strong USD/JPY 25d RR put skew of -2.20, while retail remains 71% long, providing a contrarian signal for further weakness. Fed holds at 3.75%.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Carry + Positioning + Vol
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7069, holding above the SMA20/50/200 cluster following a 1.90% gain over the last month. The pair benefits from a -71bp OIS carry premium favoring the AUD (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%), which remains a primary driver in a low-VIX (14.9) environment. COT LF net positioning is +23,616 (long% 64.1%), while retail traders are 78% short, suggesting institutional vs retail divergence that typically supports trend extension. Options pricing reflects caution with an AUD/USD VRP of +2.9% (IV 9.0% vs HV30 6.1%), indicating that while the carry trade is bid, markets are paying a significant premium for downside protection. The RBA's restrictive real rate of +0.60% vs the Fed's +1.56% narrows the restrictive gap as US yields retreat. Risk: RBA shifts to a dovish stance at the August 11 meeting, eroding the carry advantage.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance + CB Bias Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5893, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5829. The New Zealand Economic Surprise Index (ESI) is the highest in the G10 at +24.4, reflecting sustained data beats that contrast with the US ESI of -6.4. Speculative positioning remains extreme with COT LF net short -30,606 (9.7% long), which creates a significant short-squeeze risk as RBNZ remains in a 'HIKING' stance with a 2.5% policy rate. While the nominal USD/NZD carry favors USD by +125bp, the NZD real rate is deeply accommodative at -1.56%, suggesting that any hawkish shift from the RBNZ to combat inflation is likely to trigger an aggressive spec cover. Retail sentiment is 76% short, further aligning with a contrarian bullish bias for the pair. Risk: NZD/USD daily close below the 0.5829 SMA cluster nullifies the bullish technical setup.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Employment Divergence + Correlation Break
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3952, positioned below its SMA20/50 cluster of 1.4066/68. The pair is reacting to a sharp divergence in labor data as Canada added +75.1K jobs vs expectations of +15K, occurring simultaneously with the -23K US payroll miss. This fundamental divergence is testing the 133bp OIS carry advantage held by the USD (Fed 3.75% vs BoC 2.31%). Speculative positioning is heavily short CAD (COT LF net -103,684), leaving the pair sensitive to further positive CAD data surprises that could force an unwind toward the SMA200 at 1.3852. Notably, the USD/CAD vs WTI Oil correlation has weakened to a z-score of -1.14σ, indicating that CAD is currently trading more on employment and rate differentials than traditional energy price moves. Risk: WTI Oil prices fall below $70, re-establishing the traditional link and supporting USD/CAD regardless of labor data.
